questions.q: The heat of combustion of ethanol into carbon dioxides and water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>327</mn></math> Kcal at constant pressure. The heat evolved (in cal) at constant volume at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> (if all gases behave ideally) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>calmol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>________
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
C2H5OH(ℓ)+O2(g)⟶2O2(g)+3H2O(ℓ);ΔHC=-327Kcal
ΔHc=ΔUC+ΔngRT
-327×103=ΔUC+1×2×300
ΔUC=-326400 cal

So heat evolved as constant volume is 326400cal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given R=8.314 JK–1 mol–1

32O2g⇌O3g. Kp=2.47×10-29

Standard Gibbs free energy of the formation of a compound is basically the change of Gibbs free energy that is followed by the formation of one mole of that substance from its component element available at their standard states or the most stable form of the element which is at 25°C  and 100 kPa. Its symbol is ΔfG˚.

∆rG0=-RT ln Kp

=-8.314×10–3×298×ln (2.47×10–29)

=–8.314×10–3×298×(–65.87)

=163.19 kJ

questions.q:
The incorrect statements from the following is:
A. The electrical work that a reaction can perform at constant pressure and temperature is equal to the reaction Gibbs energy.
B. Ecell∘  is dependent on the pressure.
C. dEcell°dT=ΔrS°nF
D. A cell is operating reversibly if the cell potential is exactly balanced by an opposing source of potential difference.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ecell∘ is dependent on the equilibrium constant, K, which is not dependent on the pressure of any gas involved in the cell. Relation between Electrochemical Cell Potential and Gibbs free Energy change is given by; Δ G = -nFE where Delta G is Gibbs Free energy change , n is the number of electrons involved in the reaction and F is Faraday and E is the Cell potential.

We know that,

dG=VdP-SdT

At constant pressure dP=0

⇒dG=-SdT

S=-dGdT∆S=-∆dGdTP

⇒dEcell°dT=∆SnF

A cell is operating reversibly if the cell potential is exactly balanced by an opposing source of potential difference.
